text:
akshay: hey all 5 starting my first PR and want to follow team norms. quick Qs: branch naming, tiny vs big PR split guidance, commit subject format, and who to ping for a fast sanity check?
nadia: welcome! Branch: feature/ENG-9999-short-desc or fix/ENG-9999-short-desc. Keep everything kebab-case after the ticket.
ron: PR size: prefer small (<= 300 LOC) but if you must, split mechanical changes (formatting, rename) into one PR and behavior changes into another. Makes reviews much easier.
akshay: commit subject examples? we have a few styles floating around
nadia: we do a lightweight conventional style: `feat(cache): add prefix shard (ENG-9999)` or `fix(api): handle 429 backoff`. Either put the ticket in subject or first line of body.
ron: preflight: run `./scripts/preflight.sh` which runs linters, type checks, and unit tests. If preflight fails in CI due to transient infra, push an empty commit: `git commit --allow-empty -m "ci: rerun" && git push`.
akshay: some tests hit remote services and fail in CI. Is it okay to open PR with failing integration tests if I document the flakes?
nadia: yes open it and mark tests flaky in the PR body with steps to reproduce locally. Add `@eng-oncall` if you need a CI rerun. Don't merge until green unless it's a docs-only change.
preflight-bot: [preflight] Please ensure branch is up to date with main and pre-commit passes.
akshay: reviewers: who do I request for runtime library changes?
ron: check CODEOWNERS. For runtime libs ping `@team-runtime` and tag `@ron` if you want a quick look. Approval rule: 1 CODEOWNER OR 2 reviewers. Security-affecting changes need `@sec-eng` signoff.
akshay: labels and checklist to include?
nadia: paste this minimal checklist in your PR body:
```
- [ ] Summary
- [ ] Ticket: ENG-9999
- [ ] How to test locally
- [ ] CI status / flakiness notes
- [ ] Labels: area/* type/* size/*
```

akshay: thanks, I'll open a Draft PR and ping `@ron` for a quick pre-review before requesting formal reviews. appreciated!
